# 1 Chronicles Chapter 8 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 375r–375v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1CH_008_page_001.jpg, 1CH_008_page_002.jpg

---

**8:1** And-Binyamin fathered Bela his-firstborn, Ashbel the-second, and-Achirach the-third, **8:2** Nochah the-fourth, and-Rafa the-fifth. **8:3** And-there-were to-Bela sons: Addar, and-Gera, and-Avihud, **8:4** and-Avishu'a, and-Na'aman, and-Acho'ach, **8:5** and-Gera, and-Shefufan, and-Churam.

**8:6** And-these [are] the-sons of-Echud — they [are] heads of-fathers to-the-inhabitants of-Geva, and-they-exiled-them [vayyaglum] to-Manachat: **8:7** and-Na'aman, and-Achiyyah, and-Gera — he exiled-them and-he-fathered Uzza and-Achichud.

**8:8** And-Shacharayim fathered in-the-field of-Mo'av, after his-sending-away [shallecho] Chushim and-Ba'ara, his-wives. **8:9** And-he-fathered from-Chodesh his-wife: Yovav, and-Tsivya, and-Mesha, and-Malkam, **8:10** and-Ye'uts, and-Sokhyah, and-Mirmah. These [were] his-sons, heads of-fathers. **8:11** And-from-Chushim he-fathered Avituv, and-Elpa'al.

**8:12** And-the-sons of-Elpa'al: Ever, and-Mish'am, and-Shemed — he built Ono and-Lod and-its-daughters [benoteyha]. **8:13** And-Beri'ah, and-Shema — they [were] the-heads of-fathers to-the-inhabitants of-Ayyalon; they drove-out [hivrichu] the-inhabitants of-Gat.

**8:14** And-Achyo, Shashaq, and-Yeremot, **8:15** and-Zevadyah, and-Arad, and-Eder, **8:16** and-Mikha'el, and-Yishpah, and-Yocha — the-sons of-Beri'ah. **8:17** And-Zevadyah, and-Meshullam, and-Chizqi, and-Chever, **8:18** and-Yishmerai, and-Yizli'ah, and-Yovav — the-sons of-Elpa'al.

**8:19** And-Yaqim, and-Zikhri, and-Zavdi, **8:20** and-Elyo'enai, and-Tsilletai, and-Eli'el, **8:21** and-Adayah, and-Berayah, and-Shimrat — the-sons of-Shim'i. **8:22** And-Yishpan, and-Ever, and-Eli'el, **8:23** and-Avdon, and-Zikhri, and-Chanan, **8:24** and-Chananyah, and-Eilam, and-Antotiyyah, **8:25** and-Yifdeya, and-Penu'el — the-sons of-Shashaq.

**8:26** And-Shamshrai, and-Shecharyah, and-Atalyah, **8:27** and-Ya'areshyah, and-Eliyyah, and-Zikhri — the-sons of-Yerocham.

**8:28** These [were] heads of-fathers according-to-their-generations, heads — these dwelt in-Yerushalayim.

**8:29** And-in-Giv'on dwelt the-father of-Giv'on, and-the-name of-his-wife [was] Ma'akhah. **8:30** And-his-son the-firstborn [was] Avdon, and-Tsur, and-Qish, and-Ba'al, and-Nadav, **8:31** and-Gedor, and-Achyo, and-Zekher. **8:32** And-Miqlot fathered Shim'ah. And-also they, opposite their-brothers, dwelt in-Yerushalayim, with-their-brothers.

**8:33** And-Ner fathered Qish, and-Qish fathered Sha'ul, and-Sha'ul fathered Yehonatan, and-Malkishu'a, and-Avinadav, and-Eshba'al. **8:34** And-the-son of-Yehonatan [was] Meriv-Ba'al, and-Meriv-Ba'al fathered Mikhah.

**8:35** And-the-sons of-Mikhah: Piton, and-Melekh, and-Ta'area, and-Achaz. **8:36** And-Achaz fathered Yeho'addah, and-Yeho'addah fathered Alemet, and-Azmavet, and-Zimri. And-Zimri fathered Motsa. **8:37** And-Motsa fathered Bin'a; Rafah his-son, El'asah his-son, Atsel his-son.

**8:38** And-to-Atsel [were] six sons, and-these [are] their-names: Azriqam, Bokhru, and-Yishma'el, and-She'aryah, and-Ovadyah, and-Chanan. All these [were] the-sons of-Atsel.

**8:39** And-the-sons of-Esheq his-brother: Ulam his-firstborn, Ye'ush the-second, and-Elifelet the-third. **8:40** And-the-sons of-Ulam were men, mighty-ones of-valor [gibborei chayil], bending [dorkhei] bow, and-multiplying [marbei] sons and-sons of-sons — one hundred and-fifty. All these [were] from the-sons of-Binyamin.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.33 — Eshbaal:** The Chronicler preserves the original theophoric name *Eshba'al* ("man of Baal" or "fire of Baal"), which the author of Samuel changed to *Ish-boshet* ("man of shame") to avoid the Baal element. Similarly, *Meriv-Ba'al* (v.34) appears as *Mephiboshet* in Samuel.

**v.29 — "the father of Gibeon":** The Chronicler does not name this figure here, but in the parallel at 9:35 he is called *Ye'i'el* (Jeiel). This may be a scribal omission.

**v.8 — "after his sending away":** The piel infinitive *shallecho* suggests Shaharaim divorced his wives — a rare and notable detail. He then remarried in Moab, producing a new family line.

**v.12 — Shemed built Ono and Lod:** These towns (in the coastal plain) appear again in Ezra 2:33 and Nehemiah 7:37 as post-exilic settlements. The Chronicler traces their founding to pre-exilic Benjamin.

*— EMET*
